svg.title: Azure Backup Server protecting VMware VMs to a Recovery Services vault
svg.desc: Azure Backup Server protecting on-premises VMware virtual machines through vCenter, keeping the first copy on local disk and sending recovery points to a Recovery Services vault in Azure. A free-form drawing with 9 outlined areas: On-premises datacenter; VMware vSphere environment; ESXi host; ESXi host; vCenter VM folder; MABS server (Windows Server VM); Other production servers; Azure; Key. It holds 17 labelled items joined by 11 black arrows; dashed arrows are optional, standby or asynchronous paths. Arrow labels: TCP 443; TCP 443 and 902; Online backup; Restore; Agent-based; DPMDB backup to Azure; Traffic or data path; Optional or restore; Two-way link. Green numbered circles on arrows match the numbered notes under the drawing.

text.tspan: Not supported: vApps, VMs with existing
vSphere 6.5 to 8.0 with MABS v4; 9.0 needs
Windows file server with the MABS

MABS needs no agent on vCenter or the ESXi hosts. It talks to vCenter over HTTPS on TCP 443, using a VMware account that holds a role with only the privileges backup needs. Where vCenter manages the ESXi
hosts, add vCenter, not the hosts, to the protection group. For HTTPS, import the VMware CA certificate on the MABS server.

MABS reads the VM data from the ESXi hosts over TCP 443 and TCP 902 and keeps it first on local disk, in a storage pool that can be direct attached storage, a Fibre Channel SAN or iSCSI storage. A vCenter
VM folder can be protected as one unit and new VMs in it are picked up daily.
The protection group sets the short-term disk retention. The MARS agent that runs on the MABS server then backs up the MABS disks to the Recovery Services vault.
Online protection sends recovery points from MABS to the vault on the schedule you set. There is no time limit on retention; the limit is 9999 recovery points per protected instance.
For recovery you can restore the whole VM or, for Windows VMs, files and folders without restoring the whole VM. Recovery goes through MABS.

Machines outside VMware, such as a physical Windows file server, run the MABS protection agent and back up to the same MABS server. Linux VMs on VMware are protected as a whole VM, with file-consistent
The MABS database, DPMDB, holds the MABS configuration and backup data. Back it up to Azure too, so any MABS server registered in the vault can recover it.
